title: Phase 2 - Compensation Flow - Invoice Doc, Receivable/Liabilities

storage.value:
Compensations Diagram

Compensation Integration During Billing Process:

Only for Standard Billing which is only for Product Contract

  • During the billing process, when the invoice amount (deducted interim amount) is finalized, the system identifies relevant compensations for the Customer and PODs associated with the billing run.

  • Compensations are grouped by their Period (defined as a month) to ensure proper organization in the invoice PDF.

Currency Conversion:

  • If a compensation's currency differs from the system currency, it is converted to the system currency using the applicable exchange rates and then summed by their period

  • The converted compensations are then included in the invoice PDF (not in the invoice object).

Invoice PDF Data Structure:

  1. Summary Data:

    • Compensations are grouped by the Period (month).

    • Each period includes a list of PODs associated with the compensations.

    • All compensations for the same period are summed into a single value, which is displayed in the summary section.

  2. Detailed Data:

    • Compensations are grouped by POD.

    • All compensations for the same POD and Period are written separately, which are displayed in the detailed section divided into periods (months)

Regeneration of Invoice PDF:

System takes Customer and PoDs from the invoice, goes to compensations’ listing and searches for Compensations with this Customer and PoD and uses them to regenerate PDF with the same logic as it was while generation

  • The Regenerate action allows the user to update the invoice PDF.

  • During regeneration:

    • The system re-evaluates compensations for the Customer and PODs, considering the billing run data and any new compensations added since the initial generation.

    • Changes in compensations may result in updates to both Summary Data and Detailed Data:

      • Summary Data: Groups may change if new compensations are added with different periods.

      • Detailed Data: Changes may occur if compensations with different PODs are added or removed.

    • These updates are reflected in the regenerated invoice PDF.

We don’t delete old invoice pdf from the system, just from the invoice sub object, it will stay in email communication data as doc

Compensation Flow for Receivables and Liabilities + Offsetting

1. Post Billing Run Completion

  • System Action: After the billing run completes, the system generates the PDF invoice, creating a liability for the customer based on the invoice amount.

2. Compensation Search

  • System Action: The system now searches for compensations related to the customer and the Points of Delivery (PODs) involved in the billing run.

    • Search Logic:

      • The system identifies the customer and the associated PODs from the billing run.

      • The system then looks for compensations that are linked to these customers and PODs.

      • Condition: The compensations should be in "Uninvoiced" status

3. Compensation Summing

  • System Action: The system sums the amounts of all compensations that match the identified customer and PODs, grouping them by the compensation period.

    • Calculation: Compensations from the same period are added together, creating a total compensation amount for the customer in that period (for different pods)

Search and Summing Logic Example:

  • Billing Run Identifies Customer X and PODs 001, 002.

  • Compensation Table Search:

    • The system searches for compensations linked to Customer X and PODs 001 and 002.

    • Only compensations with the status "uninvoiced" will be selected.

    • These compensations are then grouped based on their period.

    • The system sums the compensation amounts for each relevant period.

4. Liability Creation for Recipient (Government)

  • System Action: For each compensation identified and grouped by period, the system creates a liability for the recipient (e.g., government).

    • Initial Liability Amount: The liability amount corresponds to the summed compensation for the customer and period.

    • Current Liability Amount: Will be the same as initial amount

    • for created customer liability details: Customer liability automatic creation (Government compensation)

5. Receivable Creation for Customer

  • System Action: The system creates a receivable for the customer with the same summed amount of compensation, representing what the customer is owed.

    • Receivable Amount: This is equal to the total compensation amount for the period.

6. Offsetting Liabilities and Receivables

  • System Action: After creating both liabilities and receivables for the customer, the system offsets the receivable for the customer (created based on compensation) with the liability for the customer (created due to the invoice amount).

    • Offset Logic:

      • The system identifies the liability created for the invoice amount and offsets it with the corresponding compensation receivable.

      • After the offset, the liability and receivable balances are reduced accordingly.

7. Updating Compensation Table

  • System Action: The system updates the compensations that were used to create the liabilities and receivables:

    • For each compensation used in the flow, the system sets its index to "0", indicating that it has been processed and applied.

    • Created Liability for Recipient will be attached to every compensation which were used

    • Created Receivable for Customer will be attached to every compensation which were used

    • Invoice will be attached to the compensations which were used for generating invoice PDF

IN OFFSET THIS INVOICE AMOUNT LIABILITY IS ALWAYS PRIORITY WHICH MEANS IF THERE IS ANOTHER LIABILITIES FOR CUSTOMER TO COVER IT WILL BE OFFSETTED AFTER ALL THIS PROCESS IS DONE (E.G INTERIM LIABILITY)

Creating Reverse Receivables and Liabilities + Offsetting

1. Update Compensation Index

  • System Action:

    • The system searches for compensations with the status "uninvoiced" linked to the invoice.

    • The index of these compensations is updated to 1.

    • For every subsequent regeneration for the same invoice, the index increases by 1 (e.g., the next regeneration would set it to 3, and so on).

Search for Compensations with Previous Index Linked to the Invoice

2. Identify Period Groups and Group Amounts

  • System Action:

    • The system retrieves compensations with the previous index linked to the invoice.

    • The compensations are grouped by period, and their amounts are summed for each period group.

Create Financial Records for Each Period Group

3. Create Liabilities for Customer

  • System Action:

    • For each period group, the system creates a liability for the customer.

    • Initial Amount: Matches the initial amount in the corresponding receivable.

    • Current Amount: Initially set equal to the initial amount.

4. Create Receivables for Recipient

  • System Action:

    • For each period group, the system creates a receivable for the recipient (e.g., government).

    • Initial Amount: Matches the initial amount in the corresponding liability.

    • Current Amount: Initially set equal to the initial amount.

5. Create New Receivable for Customer

  • System Action:

    • The system creates a new receivable for the customer based on the new compensation period group amount.

6. Create New Liability for Recipient

  • System Action:

    • The system creates a new liability for the recipient based on the new compensation period group amount.

7. Updating Compensation Table

  • System Action: The system updates the compensations that were used before and after regeneration to create the liabilities and receivables:

    • For each compensation used in the flow after reverse, the system sets its index to "1", indicating that it has been processed and applied for new generation.

    • Created Liability for Customer due to regeneration will be attached to every compensation which was with index 0

    • Created Receivable for Recipient due to regeneration will be attached to every compensation which was with index 0

    • Created Liability for Recipient will be attached to every compensation which were created after reverse with new amount (index 1)

    • Created Receivable for Customer will be attached to every compensation which were created after reverse with new amount (index 1)

Offsetting Transactions (Offset Example)

7. Offset Liability for Invoice with Customer Receivable (Index 1)

  • System Action:

    • The liability created for the invoice is offset against the receivable for the customer that was created due to compensation (index 0).

8. Offset Liability for Customer (Index 0 Reverse)

  • System Action:

    • The liability for the customer (index 0 reverse) is offset against the receivable for the customer (index 1).

    • This balances the reversed liability and customer receivable created in the previous steps.

9. Offset Receivable for Customer (Index 1)

  • System Action:

    • The receivable for the customer (index 1), created during the regeneration process, is offset against the liability for the customer (index 0 reverse).

    • This ensures all new financial records are aligned with the regenerated compensations.

Summary of the Regeneration Process

  1. Update Compensation Index:

    • Compensations with status "uninvoiced" are updated to index 1 (or higher for subsequent regenerations).

  2. Search for Previous Compensations:

    • The system retrieves compensations with the previous index and identifies their period groups.

  3. Create Financial Records:

    • For each period group, the system:

      • Creates liabilities for the customer.

      • Creates receivables for the recipient.

      • Creates a new receivable for the customer.

      • Creates a new liability for the recipient.

  4. Offsetting Transactions:

    • The system offsets:

      • The invoice liability with the customer receivable (index 0).

      • The customer liability (index 0 reverse) with the customer receivable (index 0).

      • The customer receivable (index 1) with the customer liability (index 1 reverse).
